content: 1. Tetanus toxoid, whether adsorbed or in fluid form, is contraindicated when pharmacodynamic antagonism is present. Corticosteroids increase the risk of infection when administered with live vaccines. Budesonide reduces the efficacy of the tick-borne encephalitis vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism and is contraindicated. 2. Budesonide decreases the effects of travelers' diarrhea and cholera vaccines (inactivated) via pharmacodynamic antagonism and is contraindicated. Corticosteroids also elevate the risk of infection with live vaccines. 3. Budesonide reduces the effects of the typhoid polysaccharide vaccine and the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism, making co-administration contraindicated. Corticosteroids further increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 4. Budesonide diminishes the efficacy of the varicella virus vaccine (live) and the yellow fever vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism, and their use together is contraindicated. Corticosteroids also heighten the risk of infection with live vaccines. 5. Budesonide reduces the effects of the zoster vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism, and co-administration is contraindicated. Corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 6. Budesonide and aceclofenac or acemetacin may mutually increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an elevated risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of almotriptan and alprazolam by influencing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 9. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of amiodarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while amiodarone increases budesonide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Amobarbital, butabarbital, and butalbital reduce the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of cilostazol, cinacalcet, and clozapine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Danazol increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Drugs like calcium carbonate, cimetidine, and citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 19. Co-administration of corticosteroids with anticoagulants such as antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, argatroban, bemiparin, bivalirudin, or dalteparin may decrease anticoagulant effects by increasing blood coagulability. Conversely, corticosteroids may impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. Close monitoring of INR is recommended. 20. Drugs like aprepitant, atazanavir, atorvastatin, and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal forms) and cortisone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Crizotinib and crofelemer increase the levels of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of co-administered drugs metabolized by CYP3A may be necessary. Crofelemer inhibits CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 23. Co-administration of danicopan with budesonide increases plasma concentrations of P-glycoprotein substrates. Dose reduction of P-glycoprotein substrates may be necessary where minimal concentration changes could lead to serious adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised.
